title: Site comparison preserves and detects Tor intervals
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $K\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{Et}},A)$ in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use the full small pro-etale site and its ordinary derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the comparison inverse image $\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], applied termwise on derived categories [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. For integers $a\leq b$, $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if $\nu_T^*K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Thus the test is against every module sheaf on the respective site, with no constructibility or etale-origin restriction on the pro-etale test sheaves.

proof.text: Translate the etale explicit homology-vanishing predicate into the standard t-structure-based Tor predicate using the source lemma AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn (Finiteness.FlatModel), proved via DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff. Use the existing source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_iff for exact faithful monoidal comparison. Finally use the intrinsic presentation-transport theorem to identify its right-hand side with the precise recorded predicate. The source theorem already implements flat-model preservation and tensor/conservative reflection on all test sheaves, so no unit-level step is bypassed.

proof_origin.place: torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_iff, followed by intrinsic coefficient realization transport. The source result realizes the same blueprint lemma in fixed coefficients.
